Title: March 5, 2026 - Regular City Council Meeting (Boulder City Council)
Overview: The council heard extensive open comment on Flock Safety license-plate-reader cameras and on funding and future of the South Boulder Rec Center, declined to call up the Frontier Avenue concept plan, and approved the consent agenda (excluding item 3E, which was revised for staff direction) along with the 2026 board and commission appointments effective immediately for the Boulder Urban Renewal Authority. The meeting closed with a city staff presentation on affordable housing, prompting questions on cash-in-lieu, middle-income ownership, and the 15% affordable housing goal.

Topic1.Title: Open Comment: Flock Safety Cameras
Topic1.Summary: Multiple residents urged the council to cancel or not renew the Flock Safety contract, citing ICE data-sharing concerns, racial profiling, security vulnerabilities, and reported misuse in other jurisdictions. Speakers asked for on-premises data storage alternatives and a surveillance-technology policy. Council members acknowledged the concerns and said staff is working on near-term contract decisions and a broader policy.

Topic2.Title: Open Comment: South Boulder Rec Center
Topic2.Summary: Many speakers, including seniors, swimmers, parents, and a 10-year-old, urged funding to keep the South Boulder Rec Center open with its pool and gym. Speakers raised concerns about pool consolidation, aging infrastructure, and the 15-minute neighborhood goal. An engineering challenge and a petition for a retrofit commission were also presented.

Topic3.Title: Staff Responses and Council Comments on Open Comment
Topic3.Summary: Staff said a April 9 study session will cover facilities funding and rec centers, and that Flock conversations are ongoing. The city attorney noted operations fall under the city manager, while council can set surveillance and privacy policy. Council members thanked speakers and encouraged continued civic participation, with speakers not selected being prioritized next meeting.

Topic4.Title: Consent Agenda and Item 3E Revision
Topic4.Summary: The council amended the agenda to add item 3J on the external audit firm. Item 3E, concerning area three planning reserve guidance, was pulled for separate discussion and revised to make housing types broader than middle-income ownership. The remaining consent agenda items were approved unanimously.

Topic5.Title: Call-Up Check-In: Frontier Avenue Concept Plan
Topic5.Summary: The council considered whether to call up a concept plan for redevelopment of 3550 and 3850 Frontier Avenue including an events venue, hotel, apartments, and commercial space. Council members noted zoning does not perfectly fit the mix of uses and expressed willingness to consider legislative changes later. The council declined to call up the project, with input to be given at site review.

Topic6.Title: Board and Commission Appointments 2026
Topic6.Summary: A public hearing was held on 2026 board and commission appointments, with two speakers offering comments. Council members nominated candidates seat by seat, using straw votes and elimination rounds to narrow finalists. All appointments were approved unanimously, with Boulder Urban Renewal Authority appointments made effective immediately after a replacement motion.

Topic7.Title: Affordable Housing Review
Topic7.Summary: Staff presented the current state of affordable housing, including the gap between stagnant area median income and rising home prices, Dr. Cog rental and ownership gaps, and the city's inclusionary housing outperformance at 37% of new development. Programs discussed include the affordable homeownership program, scattered-site acquisition, Boulder Mod, and the down payment assistance pilot. Council asked about cash-in-lieu economics, the 15% goal, unused $10 million voter-approved funds, and federal and vouchers impacts.

Topic8.Title: Closing Remarks and Community Announcement
Topic8.Summary: Council members thanked staff for the affordable housing presentation and the city manager's office was encouraged to use the memo format as a model. A council member announced a community invitation to a Ramadan event at the mosque. The meeting was closed at 9:05 p.m.
